subject.title: [Bug]: `exec` tool does not inherit `skills.entries.*.env` environment variables

question: Should explicitly configured credential-shaped `skills.entries.<skill>.env` keys be allowed into skill-owned host exec subprocesses, and what boundary should keep those same secrets out of unrelated generic exec calls?
rationale: Current code violates the documented host skill-env behavior for real users, but a broad allow-all fix changes how credentials enter executable child environments and overlaps the open generic exec secret-leak mitigation.

options.title: Allow only skill-scoped exec env
options.body: Permit user-configured per-skill env keys for that skill's own host exec context while keeping dangerous env names blocked and stripping active skill secrets from unrelated generic exec.

options.title: Require skill metadata declarations
options.body: Keep credential-shaped names blocked unless the skill manifest declares them, then update the `gog` skill metadata or package docs for this credential path.

options.title: Keep fail-closed behavior
options.body: Document that credential-shaped per-skill env names are intentionally blocked and require top-level/system env or an approved sandbox/env configuration instead.

recommendation.title: Allow only skill-scoped exec env
recommendation.body: Permit user-configured per-skill env keys for that skill's own host exec context while keeping dangerous env names blocked and stripping active skill secrets from unrelated generic exec.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice crosses the documented skill-env contract, sanitizer behavior, and host exec security posture where steipete has strong history signals.
